result.note: Mainly a protest story; tested only the concessions the Jharkhand government announced on the recruitment-exam irregularities, and the CBI demand that remains unmet.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Jharkhand government responded to protests over alleged irregularities in state recruitment examinations. Consider the following statements about the measures it agreed to:
items: It agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination.
It agreed to hand the investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
It agreed to set up a fast-track court to file charge sheets within 90 days.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The state opened a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) probe, and the protesters' central demand for a CBI probe remains unmet. TBB notes the state is wary because the CBI answers to the Centre, run by the BJP, which is Jharkhand's opposition.
questions.source: Jharkhand's higher education minister, Sudivya Kumar Sonu, said on Sunday the state has agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC preliminary examination and the 2023-25 backlog exams, open a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) probe, seek an Enforcement Directorate (ED) investigation into alleged financial irregularities, and set up a fast-track court to file charge sheets within 90 days.
